resources.string: Say the Goal reads the controls on screen and taps, types and scrolls for you when you ask by voice. It acts only in Gmail, Calendar, Chrome and Messages, and asks before anything is submitted or sent.
Set up once. After that, just say what you need.
Say \"Hey Goal\", then what you want. For example: \"Hey Goal, find the library workshop invite and register me.\" Say \"Stop\" at any time.
This lets the app read the screen and tap for you. In the list that opens, choose Say the Goal (it may be under Installed apps), then switch it on.
So the app can hear \"Hey Goal\" and your answers. Choose \"While using the app\".
So the app can pick times that don\'t clash with your events. It only reads your calendar.
So the app can find the photo you ask for. Choose \"Allow all\".
So the app can show that it is listening.
Press the button, then say: \"Hey Goal, what do you remember?\" The app should answer out loud.
Listening for 30 seconds. Say: \"Hey Goal, what do you remember?\"
It didn\'t hear \"Hey Goal\". Move closer to the phone and try again.
Finish the steps above first: turn on Say the Goal and allow the microphone.
Debug build: adb hooks are active while the service is on.
These are the choices you asked the app to remember. It uses them so it doesn\'t have to ask you again. You can remove any of them.
The app only remembers what you tell it to. When it asks you a question, add \"remember that\" to your answer. For example: \"Email. Remember that for event signups.\"
\"%1$s\" will be forgotten. The app will ask you again next time.
